body.statement: Can \(\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{comp}}\) construct, for every \(n\ge2\), two finite priors supported on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) whose target values are separated by at least \(c\rho_n\) and whose actual fixed-\(n\) product mixtures have squared Hellinger distance at most \(1/4\)? The required certificate must prove exact equality of every singleton conditional mixture, the uniform component inequality \(H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le C a^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r\) for every \(r\ge2\), and the full graph sum \(H^2(\int P_\vartheta^{\otimes n}d\Pi_+,\int P_\vartheta^{\otimes n}d\Pi_-)\le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\), without support deletion, conditioning on a favorable occupancy event, or Poissonization without an exact reduction.
body.justification: This is the load-bearing new proof object: one-observation cancellation alone does not control a shared-prior product likelihood.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE deletes transition-region support, while RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax requires partition-local perturbations; neither covers overlapping smooth frames under exact uniform support.
body.consumer: A successful component certificate is reusable for nonlinear-functional lower bounds whenever full random-design support prevents partition-local cancellation.
